text: In 1930, buying a home looked like this.
A bank lent about half the price.
You had three to five years.
Then the whole loan came due, all at once.
No new loan? You could lose the house.
In December 1930, New York's Bank of United States closed.
In 1931, its depositors still crowded outside.
It insured a new kind of loan: up to eighty percent of the value,
paid down every month, for up to twenty years.
No giant bill at the end.
In 1954, the limit stretched to thirty years.
The long, monthly mortgage starts here.
